manuscript.title: A negative solution to the complemented subspace problem for Banach spaces with unconditional bases
manuscript.display_title: A NEGATIVE SOLUTION TO THE COMPLEMENTED SUBSPACE PROBLEM FOR BANACH SPACES WITH UNCONDITIONAL BASES
manuscript.abstract_tex:
We give a negative solution to the complemented subspace problem for Banach spaces with unconditional bases over both the real and complex fields. For every $\rho>0$, we construct a projection $P_\rho$ of norm less than $1+\rho$ on a separable superreflexive space
\[
X_\rho=\left(\bigoplus_{j=1}^{\infty}\ell_{p_j}^{N_j}\right)_2,\qquad p_j\downarrow2,
\]
such that $Z_\rho=P_\rho(X_\rho)$ and its dual $Z_\rho^*$ have Schauder bases but admit no unconditional bases. Over the real field, both spaces have Gordon–Lewis local unconditional structure (GL-lust) but fail Dubinsky–Pełczyński–Rosenthal local unconditional structure (DPR-lust), disproving a conjecture of Figiel, Johnson and Tzafriri. In particular, neither is isomorphic to a Banach lattice, giving a negative solution to the separable Banach-lattice complemented subspace problem. A modification of the construction also shows that the class of separable real Banach lattices is not primary. A Lean 4 formalisation of the main results accompanies the paper.

results.statement_tex:
For every $\rho>0$, there exist sequences $(N_j)_{j=1}^{\infty}$ in $\mathbb N$ and $(p_j)_{j=1}^{\infty}$ in $(2,3]$, with $p_j\downarrow2$, and a projection $P_\rho$ on the separable superreflexive real Banach lattice
\[
X_\rho=\left(\bigoplus_{j=1}^{\infty}\ell_{p_j}^{N_j}(\mathbb R)\right)_2
\]
such that, with $Z_\rho=P_\rho(X_\rho)$:
(i) for $V\in\{Z_\rho,Z_\rho^*\}$,
\[
\chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(V)\leq\|P_\rho\|<1+\rho,\qquad\chi_{\mathrm{DPR}}(V)=\infty;
\]
(ii) $P_\rho$ can be chosen so that $\|I-P_\rho\|<1+\rho$ and (i) also holds for $(I-P_\rho)(X_\rho)$ and its dual, with $P_\rho$ replaced by $I-P_\rho$.
results.correspondence: Quantifiers, block parameters, idempotence, both strict norm bounds, and all four GL/DPR range and continuous-dual clauses match. Geometry is encoded differently as described below.
results.lean_statement_tex: The displayed Theorem A with the ambient superreflexivity clause replaced by uniform convexity of the existing $\ell_2(\ell_{p_j}^{N_j})$ norm. Equivalently, for each $Q\in\{P,I-P\}$ and $V\in\{Q(X),Q(X)^*\}$, $\chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(V)\leq\|Q\|$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{DPR}}(V)=\infty$, with $\|P\|,\|I-P\|<1+\rho$.
caveats: The exact Lean target says UniformConvexSpace, not a separately defined superreflexivity predicate. The manuscript also proves uniform convexity in Corollary 4.2(ii), p.20. The project does not prove the general equivalence with the finite-representability definition of superreflexivity.
Lean indexes blocks by 0,1,... and uses positive natural dimensions. Its antitone exponent condition means nonincreasing convergence to 2; do not restate it as strictly decreasing.
The main target does not itself include basis existence or nonlattice conclusions. Separate real corollary theorems establish those conclusions.

results.statement_tex: For $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and every $\rho>0$, there are a Banach space $X_\rho$ over $\mathbb K$ with a $1$-unconditional basis and a projection $P_\rho$ on $X_\rho$ with $\|P_\rho\|<1+\rho$ such that, writing $Z_\rho=P_\rho(X_\rho)$, neither $Z_\rho$ nor $Z_\rho^*$ admits an unconditional basis. If $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$, neither space is isomorphic to a Banach lattice.
results.correspondence: realCorollary matches the real case including both universal nonlattice negations. realUnconditionalCorollary extracts the real basis-only case. complexCorollary matches the complex case via ComplexCorollaryStatement = UnconditionalCorollaryStatement ℂ.
caveats: Negative basis predicates include finite bases (including the empty zero-space basis) and natural-number-indexed bases. The ambient witness is an infinite 1-unconditional Schauder basis.
Over the complex field 1-unconditional means contractivity for all complex multipliers of modulus at most 1, including phases.

Theorem B itself and these Lean theorem statements do not include conditional Schauder-basis existence, shrinking/bounded completeness, tail basis constants, or the strict lower projection bound 1 < ||P||.
The complex theorem does not state complex GL/DPR constants or nonisomorphism to a complex Banach lattice. Real chiGL/chiDPR must not be presented as complex predicates.

results.statement_tex: The class of separable real Banach lattices is not primary.
results.lean_statement_tex: For every $\rho>0$ there is a separable real Banach lattice $X$, isomorphic to a complete uniformly convex space, with a $1$-unconditional Schauder basis and a bounded real-linear map $P:X\to X$ such that $P^2=P$, $\|P\|<1+\rho$, $\|I-P\|<1+\rho$, and neither $P(X)$ nor $(I-P)(X)$ is isomorphic to any real Banach lattice.
results.correspondence: The theorem gives a counterexample over the real field. It does not define a general class-primary predicate. The real-field scope and detailed witness are stated in PDF Section 4.3 and Corollary 4.5, p.22.
caveats: Superreflexivity in this theorem is IsSuperreflexiveByRenorming: bounded linear isomorphism to a complete uniformly convex normed space.

results.statement_tex: For the Section 3.6 projection $P$ and $Z=P(X)$ with inherited norm: (i) $\chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(Z)\leq\|P\|<1+\rho$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{DPR}}(Z)=\infty$; $Z$ has no unconditional Schauder basis and, over $\mathbb R$, is not isomorphic to any Banach lattice. (ii) $X$ and $Z$ are uniformly convex and hence superreflexive. (iii) $Z$ has a contractive unconditional finite-dimensional decomposition and the metric approximation property.
results.correspondence: These theorems include the real local-structure conclusions, the basis exclusions and uniform convexity of the real ambient norm. They do not prove the full corollary for the manuscript’s projection.
caveats: Complex GL/DPR clauses are not in the selected Lean statements.
FDD and metric approximation property are outside selected verified theorems.
Do not claim that all Corollary 4.2 clauses occur in one exported target.

results.statement_tex: For $Z=P(X)$ as in Corollary 4.2: (i) $\chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(Z^*)\leq\|P\|<1+\rho$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{DPR}}(Z^*)=\infty$; $Z^*$ has no unconditional Schauder basis and, over $\mathbb R$, is not isomorphic to any Banach lattice. (ii) $Z^*$ is superreflexive. (iii) $Z^*$ has a contractive unconditional finite-dimensional decomposition and the metric approximation property.
results.correspondence: These theorems cover part of the result: real GL/DPR clauses for the continuous dual and real/complex dual-basis exclusions; realCorollary also excludes every real Banach lattice for the dual.
caveats: No full Corollary 4.5 theorem, no complex GL/DPR theorem, and no selected FDD/MAP or dual-superreflexivity clause.

results.statement_tex: For every $\rho>0$ there are a separable superreflexive real Banach lattice $X$ with a $1$-unconditional basis and a projection $Q$ with $\|Q\|<1+\rho$ and $\|I-Q\|<1+\rho$. Each of $QX,(I-Q)X,(QX)^*,((I-Q)X)^*$ (i) has GL-lust, fails DPR-lust, and is not isomorphic to a Banach lattice; (ii) has a contractive unconditional finite-dimensional decomposition and the metric approximation property. Consequently, the class of separable real Banach lattices is not primary.
results.correspondence: realMainTheorem gives both projection norms and all four real GL/DPR conclusions. realSeparableNonprimarity gives the geometric/basis ambient witness and nonlattice conclusions for the two complementary ranges. These Lean statements are not a single full formalisation of Corollary 4.6.
caveats: The two complementary dual nonlattice negations are not conjuncts of SeparableNonprimarityStatement; do not silently add them to that theorem.

results.statement_tex: For $Z_\rho$ of Theorem B and its dual over either scalar field, and over $\mathbb R$ also for $QX,(I-Q)X$ of Corollary 4.6 and their duals: (i) each space admits a conditional Schauder basis which is shrinking and boundedly complete; (ii) these bases may be chosen so that their restrictions to successive block tails have basis constants tending to one.
results.correspondence: Manuscript result only; explicitly outside the selected verified scope.
caveats: The abstract includes Schauder-basis existence. Reproducing the abstract is appropriate only when identified as manuscript text, not as a summary of all Lean-verified conclusions.

results.statement_tex: Over $\mathbb R$, $Z\oplus_\infty c_0$ has DPR-lust although its contractively complemented subspace $Z$ does not; hence DPR-lust is not preserved even by contractively complemented subspaces.
results.correspondence: A consequence of the stabilisation theorem cited in the manuscript, outside the selected verified theorems.

definitions.name: DPR constant
definitions.notes: Submodules with inherited norms; both outer suprema exclude zero; values in nonnegative extended reals. The infima need not be attained.

definitions.name: GL constant
definitions.statement_tex: \chi_{\mathrm{GL}}(Z)=\sup_{V\subseteq Z,\ 0<\dim V<\infty}\inf\{\|a\|\|b\|: V\xrightarrow{a}U\xrightarrow{b}Z,\ ba=\iota_V,\ U\text{ finite dimensional with a }1\text{-unconditional basis}\}.
definitions.notes: Auxiliary coordinates carry an arbitrary positive-definite norm, with infimum over certified bounds. The source converts to and from factorisations through normed spaces. The map b need not be injective. These constants are real-field definitions only.

definitions.name: Unconditional basis
definitions.statement_tex: \left\|\sum_i\theta_i b_i\otimes b_i^*\right\|\leq C\quad\text{for every finitely supported }(\theta_i),\ |\theta_i|\leq1.
definitions.notes: Finite or sequential bases count in exclusions. The ambient basis is sequential. Complex multipliers include phases, not only real signs or coordinate projections.

definitions.name: Ambient blocks
definitions.notes: Mathlib PiLp counting norms in finite blocks; outer dependent lp exponent 2. Lean indexing begins at 0. The manuscript construction also uses normalised counting norms before rescaling.

definitions.name: Range and dual
definitions.notes: Range has the inherited norm; dual is the continuous dual with operator norm. Complement GL bounds use ||I-P||, not ||P||.

definitions.name: Lattice and superreflexivity conventions
definitions.statement_tex: E\simeq L\text{ for some real Banach lattice }L;\qquad E\simeq H\text{ for some complete uniformly convex }H.
definitions.notes: Nonlattice means no bounded real-linear isomorphism to any Banach lattice model with any norm. It is not merely failure of a lattice order for the current norm. Superreflexivity is expressed by uniformly convex renormability; no finite-representability equivalence is proved.

proof_route_differences.paper: Circle/sphere function spaces and later finite-dimensional embeddings, including real circle-grid sampling and complex finite conditional expectations.
proof_route_differences.lean: Direct finite frames and finite products with normalised coefficient norms and range isometries.

proof_route_differences.paper: Gaussian coefficient vectors and tensor/fourth-moment estimates.
proof_route_differences.lean: Finite independent signs, explicit finite-sum second/fourth moments, and finite Holder interpolation; real polarisation and a 2-by-2 block induction.

proof_route_differences.paper: Cancellation in the one-factor bound near p=2 and Stern's projection-complement estimate.
proof_route_differences.lean: A scalar energy derivative and Pythagoras give a fixed four-coordinate bound 1+18(p-2)^2 and its tensor bound; elementary Hilbert geometry controls complementary projections.

proof_route_differences.paper: Quantitative local Hilbert estimates, reflexivity and Hahn-Banach quotient identifications in the dual obstruction.
proof_route_differences.lean: Compactness of normalised finite-dimensional norms and the exact parallelogram law establish the existence of the constants needed for the local Hilbert estimates; squared-evaluation arguments handle continuous duals and biduals without global reflexivity.

proof_route_differences.paper: Uses DPR-lust of real Banach lattices and invariance under isomorphism.
proof_route_differences.lean: Proves chiDPR of each real Banach lattice's continuous dual is at most one through disjoint approximation; combines primal, dual and bidual obstructions to obtain the required nonlattice statements.

proof_route_differences.paper: Complex sphere tensors and a corrected finite-dimensional embedding.
proof_route_differences.lean: Pure complex frame projection of order n_j-1; a uniform underlying-real equivalence to the real frame of order n_j, lifted to the outer sum, transfers the real DPR obstruction and its continuous-dual counterpart.

principal_caveats: Theorems A and B have no detected contradiction in the compared quantitative/basis clauses. This is not a certification of the entire manuscript.
Theorem A requires uniform convexity in Lean; nonprimarity uses uniformly convex renormability. The general analytic superreflexivity equivalences are not proved by this project.
The manuscript PDF and bundled LaTeX have wording differences, notably Corollary C. The PDF is authoritative for titles, quotes and page labels in this mapping.

The abstract includes existence of conditional Schauder bases. Corollary 5.2, FDD/MAP, stabilisation, geometric Remark 5.3, and the external sharp contractive complex theorem are outside the selected Lean statements.
Only real GL/DPR constants are defined. The complex theorem directly proves both basis exclusions.
Do not combine separate existential Lean statements into an unrecorded single stronger target, or call full Corollaries 4.2/4.5/4.6 verified on the basis of partial correspondence.
